name: Ham Fried Rice
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified 526 cal / 30g protein at the source, clears both bars with no adjustment. Every ingredient board-tracked and it is among the cheapest per-serving dinners in the pool. Distinct from the live Ground Beef Fried Rice Bowls by protein. Wok-and-divide, scales in two batches. Second use of the deli-ham commodity, which is currently dead weight on the board. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Fried rice was invented to use up yesterday's rice, and it is still the best trick in budget cooking. Diced ham, scrambled egg, carrots and green onion tossed in a hot pan with soy sauce and a finish of sesame oil. It comes together in about twenty minutes of actual cooking and lands at 28 grams of protein for about $1.51 a bowl.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 6.5 cups dry: ~$1.46. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (black pepper, salt): ~$0.14. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $21.13 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.51 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $24.68 across 14 servings, roughly $1.76 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $13.01 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $37.69. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $1.51 a bowl for takeout style fried rice made at home. A single order of this at a restaurant costs more than the entire batch of fourteen.
shop_smart: Cook the rice the day before. Cold, dried out rice fries. Fresh warm rice steams and clumps. This costs nothing and it is the difference between fried rice and rice mush.
Diced ham is the biggest line by far. Deli ends and pieces from the counter are often marked well below the packaged tubs, and they taste exactly the same once diced.
Eggs are the cheapest protein you can add to anything. A single carton carries this batch and lifts the protein number for next to nothing.
Sesame oil goes in at the end, not the start. It burns at high heat and it is expensive. Off the heat, a small amount flavors the whole pan and one bottle lasts many batches.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice the day before if you can and spread it on a sheet pan to cool and dry in the fridge overnight.
Dice the carrots small, slice the green onions and separate the white parts from the green tops, and mince the garlic.
Beat the eggs, then scramble them in a little of the vegetable oil in your largest skillet until just set. Take them out and chop them roughly.
Add more oil and fry the diced ham until the edges crisp, then add the carrots and the white parts of the green onions and cook until the carrots soften.
Add the garlic for a few seconds, then add the cold rice and press it into the hot pan. Let it sit undisturbed between stirs so it toasts instead of steaming.
Pour the soy sauce around the edges of the pan rather than into the middle so it hits hot metal and caramelizes.
Kill the heat, fold in the scrambled egg and the green onion tops, then finish with the sesame oil and black pepper.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, tossing between scoops so the ham and egg stay even. Every bowl lands near 565 calories and 28 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from spendwithpennies.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Takeout at home for about $1.51 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Ham fried rice with scrambled egg, carrots and green onion, finished with sesame oil. 14 servings, 565 calories, 28g protein, about $1.51 per serving.
head.keywords: ham fried rice, leftover ham recipe, fried rice meal prep, takeout at home, budget dinner
steps: Cook the rice ahead and chill it so it dries out before frying.
Scramble the beaten eggs in a little oil, then remove and chop them.
Fry the diced ham until crisp at the edges, then add carrots and the white parts of the green onions.
Add the garlic, then the cold rice, pressing it into the hot pan so it toasts.
Pour the soy sauce around the pan edges, fold in the egg and green onion tops, and finish with sesame oil.
